items.title: Ex-CFO grilled for third day over RM370mil plantation deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today recorded for a third consecutive day the statement of a former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body-owned company over alleged abuse of power involving the RM370 million acquisition of shares in two plantation companies. The statement-taking session at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya lasted more than seven hours. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the former senior executive arrived at the headquarters about 10am.

items.title: Brazil hits new diplomatic lows with US and Argentina
items.summary: Two months before Brazil's election, diplomatic tensions are flaring between President Lula's leftist administration and the right-wing governments of Argentina and the United States. "We cannot accept interference," leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said in an interview Wednesday, a day after the United States announced it had revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador. Both Trump and Milei are allies of Brazil's far-right Bolsonaro family.

items.title: MPV driver calls for improved LPT2 safety measures after elephant collision
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 6 — The driver of a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) that collided with a herd of wild elephants at Kilometre 274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) here last Tuesday has expressed disappointment over the highway’s safety measures, claiming they failed to prevent wild animals from entering the carriageway and endangering motorists. He said motorists using the highway face the risk of even more serious accidents if elephants and other wild animals continue to breach the expressway in future. He therefore supported Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi’s directive yesterday for the LPT2 concessionaire to immediately repair damaged safety fencing and review long-term measures to enhance motorists’ safety following the incident.

items.title: Malaysia launches anti-dumping probe, reviews steel import duties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has launched an anti-dumping investigation into certain coated steel imports from China, Chinese Taipei and Vietnam, alongside an expiry review of existing duties on prepainted steel coil imports from China and Vietnam. The actions follow petitions from local steel manufacturers, who claimed unfairly priced imports continue to harm Malaysia's domestic steel industry, the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said. One petitioner, NS Bluescope Malaysia Sdn Bhd, sought an investigation into imports of flat-rolled alloy and non-alloy steel products plated or coated with aluminium and zinc from China, Chinese Taipei and Vietnam.

items.title: AWC lands third data centre plumbing job in 12 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AWC Bhd has secured a RM23.1 million subcontract for plumbing, silo tank and internal sanitary works at a data centre project, marking its engineering division's third data centre contract in the past 12 months. Group chief executive officer and president Datuk Ahmad Kabeer Mohamed Nagoor said the latest award reflected customers' confidence in AWC's ability to deliver specialised works for data centre projects. He said securing three data centre contracts over the past year demonstrated that the segment had become a consistent and growing source of work for the engineering division.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: KL’s rising startup ranking just the beginning as Malaysia eyes lasting growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Malaysia’s startup ecosystem has climbed into the world’s 31st to 40th bracket, but Economy Minister Datuk Seri Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the government’s priority is building a sustainable ecosystem rather than chasing higher rankings. Akmal said Kuala Lumpur is now ranked 31st among the world’s startup ecosystems, up from 47th two years ago. “At the same time, we want to establish the startup ecosystem as one of the country’s key strengths.

items.title: Foreign investors return to Malaysian equities in July with RM301mil net inflows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors returned to Malaysian equities in July with RM300.9 million in net inflows, ending two consecutive months of selling. Buying interest centred on financial services, transportation and logistics, and utilities sectors, according to MBSB Research's latest weekly fund flow report. The return of foreign buying was selective, with industrial products and services recording RM759.7 million in net outflows, while technology saw RM484.9 million in foreign selling.

items.title: Na'imah wins bid to quash RM313.8mil tax demand
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid has succeeded in her legal challenge to set aside the Inland Revenue Board's (IRB) demand for RM313.8 million in additional tax. High Court judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad allowed Na'imah's judicial review application, ruling that the IRB director-general's decision to impose additional tax for the 2018 year of assessment was tainted by illegality and irrationality. After the proceedings, Na'imah's lawyer Datuk S. Saravana Kumar said his client felt vindicated.

items.title: Pakistan restricts international media reporting outside main cities
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan's government has instructed international media to register journalists and seek permission for any reporting outside the country's three main cities, sparking concern from rights and media groups over a threat to press freedom. The information ministry sent a statement on Monday to an international media message group on the requirement to seek permission for reporting outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi. Written guidelines published by the ministry stated all journalists working for international media, including freelance reporters, should register with the government's external media wing.

items.title: Kuala Lumpur police reshuffle six senior positions including CID, narcotics and district chiefs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus today witnessed a handover of duties ceremony involving six senior positions within the Kuala Lumpur police contingent at the Kuala Lumpur police contingent ceadquarters. The ceremony was also attended by Kuala Lumpur deputy police chief Datuk Mohd Azani Omar. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus (centre) witnesses the handover of duties as Sentul district police chief from ACP Basri Sagoni (left) to Supt Jasni Zolpa at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters, August 6, 2026.

items.title: KL20 Summit goes nationwide with Penang, Johor stops as Malaysia ramps up startup ambitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The KL20 Summit will expand beyond the capital this year, with events scheduled in Penang, Johor and Kuala Lumpur as Putrajaya seeks to strengthen regional innovation ecosystems while advancing its ambition of making Malaysia a leading startup hub. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the summit will be held as a three-city series, beginning in Penang on Sept 24, followed by Johor on Sept 29, before culminating in Kuala Lumpur on Nov 5. “KL20 2026 will be held across three strategic locations — Penang, Johor and Kuala Lumpur — in collaboration with key strategic partners including Khazanah Nasional Berhad, KWAP, NCIA and IRDA.

items.title: Afghan man given life sentence for deadly Munich car-ramming
items.summary: MUNICH: A German court on Thursday handed a life jail term to an Afghan man for a car-ramming attack in Munich last year which killed a two-year-old girl and her mother and left dozens injured. The attack was one of several committed by foreign nationals in the run-up to last year's general election that inflamed debate on immigration and security. As well as two counts of murder, Farhad N. initially faced 44 counts of attempted murder, but half of these were later replaced by counts of bodily harm, 19 of them serious.

items.title: Organisational transformation begins with people, not KPIs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Winning employees' trust and sense of purpose is the first step towards organisational transformation, says former Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) Group Chief Human Capital Officer Datuk Dr Mohd Khalis Abdul Rahim. Drawing from his experience in leading transformation efforts, he said many initiatives failed because organisations focused on restructuring, processes and performance targets before rebuilding employees' emotional connection with the workplace. He said organisations must first restore employees' sense of meaning, purpose and pride, especially when financial resources are limited and monetary incentives are not possible.

items.title: Southern Score Builders wins RM146.5mil data centre subcontract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd's unit SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd has clinched a RM146.5 million subcontract for electrical works at a data centre project. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the company said SJEE was awarded the job by a local construction company to undertake the project's Electrical Package 3 Works (Medium Voltage). Southern Score Builders has secured four data centre-related contracts worth a combined RM383.05 million so far this year.

items.title: MGB completes structural milestone for RM437mil Johor high-rise project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MGB Bhd has completed the topping-out ceremony for Pangsapuri Saujana Indah in Molek, Johor Bahru, marking the completion of the project's main structural works and bringing the developer closer to delivering its first high-rise development in Johor. The project, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM437 million, comprises two 37-storey residential towers offering 988 units. Tower A features 393 units, while Tower B comprises 595 units, with built-up areas ranging from 590 sq ft to 863 sq ft. Pangsapuri Saujana Indah is MGB's first high-rise project in Johor and its inaugural development in Johor Bahru, expanding the group's presence beyond its existing markets.

items.title: Rocky's death highlights need for humane stray animal management - activist
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The death of a dog named Rocky in Klang has highlighted the need to review existing procedures for managing stray animals to ensure enforcement operations are carried out more humanely and systematically. Community activist Michael Tay said current standard operating procedures (SOPs) may not have fully addressed public sensitivities, concerns of surrounding residents and animal welfare considerations during enforcement operations. He said every stray animal operation must be conducted without cruelty as animals were living creatures deserving of ethical treatment.

items.title: Customs Dept strengthens response to social media crises with digital training
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Exposure to digital narrative simulations is expected to enhance the ability of Customs Department personnel to manage issues and crises on social media more effectively. Royal Malaysian Customs Academy (AKMAL) Sarawak branch director Deswita Santari Abdul Khalik said it formed part of a strategic and digital media management course held in Kuching, Sarawak, from Aug 3 to 6. She said participants were guided through practical sessions on producing digital media content such as rapid response statements, media releases, social media writing, infographic design and effective press conference management.

items.title: US requests Filipino pastor's extradition on sex charges
items.summary: MANILA: The United States has formally requested the extradition of a Filipino pastor wanted on sex-trafficking charges, the Philippines' ambassador to Washington said on Thursday. Apollo Quiboloy, a self-proclaimed "Appointed Son of God" and ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in the Philippines in 2024 on human-trafficking charges. A US grand jury had indicted Quiboloy three years earlier for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children, and bulk cash smuggling.

items.title: Malaysia expands KL20 2026 focus to eight sectors to accelerate startup growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will broaden the focus of KL20 2026 from four to eight key sectors as part of efforts to strengthen the startup ecosystem and accelerate the development of higher-value, technology-driven economic activities. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said KL20 2026 would continue to prioritise four existing sectors, energy and green technology, agricultural technology, manufacturing and automation, and Islamic finance, while introducing four new areas. He said KL20 must involve the entire ecosystem including government agencies, investors, technology developers, startups, talent institutions and industry players.

items.title: Actress, company directors among 17 charged over Perkeso claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seventeen people, including company directors and an actress, pleaded not guilty today to charges involving alleged false claims under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme. In Kuala Lumpur, actress Farah Wahida Zainuddin, 44, and Mohd Nizam Jamaluddin, 45, faced four charges each before Judge Suzana Hussin, while Lim Sue Peng, 54, and Lim Sian Tze, 54, faced five and eight charges respectively before Judge Rosli Ahmad. In Perak, four business owners faced 29 charges at the Ipoh Sessions Court, while four others in Penang were charged with 30 offences at the George Town Sessions Court.

items.title: Jalan Ampang crash: Prosecution challenges bid to quash murder charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The prosecution has raised a preliminary objection to a college student's application to strike out two murder charges over a road crash that killed a married couple on Jalan Ampang near Great Eastern Mall on May 2. He told reporters this after the case was mentioned before High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin, with defence lawyer S. Selvam representing Danish Raman Kamar Kumaresan, 24. Aslam fixed Aug 17 to hear the application.

items.title: Court upholds conviction, spares man from gallows in daughter's murder
items.summary: A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Nordin Hassan, Datuk Seri Vazeer Alam Mydin Meera, and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali upheld the conviction of Mohammad Abdullah Mohamed, 44, under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Delivering the majority decision, Justice Nordin said the court found no miscarriage of justice in the earlier rulings. "The court finds no miscarriage of justice in the earlier court decision convicting the appellant.

items.title: Actress, business owners among 17 facing charges over alleged Perkeso claims scam
items.summary: The accused, comprising nine men and eight women, were charged separately over offences allegedly committed in 2024. In Kuala Lumpur, actress Farah Wahida Zainuddin, 44, and Mohd Nizam Jamaluddin, 45, each faced four charges before Judge Suzana Hussin, while Lim Sue Peng and Lim Sian Tze, both 54, were charged before Judge Rosli Ahmad with five and eight counts respectively. Assari Enterprise owner Chuah Hok Guan, 60, and AC Engineering owner Chiang Hon Wai, 44, each faced five charges, with Chuah accused of abetting Chiang.

items.title: Ministry invites stakeholder feedback to strengthen use, purchase of local products
items.summary: Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said that suggestions and views can be channelled to the ministry or relevant agencies, and they will be presented to the Cabinet Committee to empower the use and purchase of local products, which is expected to hold its first meeting soon. The committee aims to coordinate the efforts of various ministries and agencies so that they no longer operate in silos, thereby reducing dependence on imported products, increasing the contribution of local products to the country's economic growth, and assisting local entrepreneurs. He said the committee also involves the Economy Ministry, of Investment Trade and Industry Ministry (MITI); Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry, Finance Ministry, and various related agencies.

items.title: India youth protests highlight mistrust in 'lapdog' media
items.summary: In rallies across the country spearheaded by the online Cockroach Janta Party movement, protest signs branded TV channels as "India's worst enemies", and activists criticised "lapdog" media said to be aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration. At New Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site, many students said they relied on social media and independent platforms. The immediate backlash saw protesters target TV journalists.

items.title: Malaysia, Vietnam deepen defence ties amid regional challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Vietnam are set to strengthen defence cooperation through greater collaboration in military training, intelligence sharing, maritime domain awareness and emerging security challenges. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the areas were discussed during his bilateral meeting with Vietnam's Minister of National Defence General Phan Văn Giang during his two-day official visit to the country. "Various areas of cooperation were discussed, including bilateral military training, intelligence sharing, maritime domain awareness, submarine rescue operations, artificial intelligence (AI), the defence industry, and efforts to address emerging security challenges such as grey zone activities," he said in a statement.

items.title: Defence at heart of Malaysia-Canada ties as new pact takes shape
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Canada is seeking to strengthen defence ties with Malaysia as part of its broader commitment to building partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, with a bilateral defence cooperation agreement expected to be signed next year. Canadian Armed Forces Senior Military Representative-Indo-Pacific (SMR-IP) Lieutenant-General Derek Macaulay said the proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU), which has been under negotiation since 2024, was progressing well. He said the agreement would serve as a starting point for both countries to explore further opportunities to share knowledge and strengthen defence cooperation.

items.title: MPV driver laments wild elephants breaching LPT2 after collision
items.summary: CHUKAI: The driver of a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) that collided with a herd of wild elephants at Km274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) here last Tuesday has expressed disappointment over the highway's safety measures, claiming they failed to prevent wild animals from entering the carriageway and endangering motorists. He said motorists using the highway face the risk of even more serious accidents if elephants and other wild animals continue to breach the expressway in future. He therefore supported Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi 's directive yesterday for the LPT2 concessionaire to immediately repair damaged safety fencing and review long-term measures to enhance motorists' safety following the incident.

items.title: Malaysia secures RM791.5mil in Farnborough Airshow deals
items.summary: The five-day event, held from July 20 to 24, saw the Malaysia Pavilion facilitate 148 business meetings between Malaysian companies and international aerospace stakeholders, according to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade). The pavilion, coordinated by Matrade in collaboration with the National Aerospace Industry Corp Malaysia (Naico), featured 15 Malaysian exhibitors alongside Invest Selangor Bhd and the Malaysia Aerospace Industry Association (MAIA). Matrade chief executive officer Abu Bakar Yusof said the commercial outcomes reaffirmed Malaysia's competitiveness as a trusted aerospace manufacturing and supply chain partner.

items.title: Auditor General blocked from probing Najib's accounts, says Pua [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Auditor General was barred from examining Datuk Seri Najib Razak's bank accounts during its audit of 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), the High Court heard today. Former Public Accounts Committee (PAC) member Tony Pua said the restriction, coupled with 1MDB's failure to provide key documents, significantly limited the audit's scope. Testifying in 1MDB's US$5.64 billion civil suit against Najib and seven others, Pua said the Auditor General had to rely solely on 1MDB's audited financial statements and supporting documents provided by the company's external auditors.

items.title: Pacific islands alarmed by Trump-backed push for deep-sea mining
items.summary: SYDNEY: A Pacific island leader says there were "no consultations" before the US announced swathes of nearby ocean could be auctioned for deep-sea mining exploration, telling AFP the industry faced strong opposition among his people. Commonwealth of Northern Mariana Islands Governor David Apatang said the idea had caused great unease across the tropical island chain of some 40,000 people. The United States alarmed its tropical island territories earlier this year, detailing plans to carve up parts of the Pacific Ocean for mining exploration.

items.title: Fahmi says Unity govt remains stable despite Johor, Negeri Sembilan political developments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Cooperation among parties in the Unity Government remains strong and stable despite political developments in states including Johor and Negeri Sembilan, according to Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesman, said state-level political developments had nothing to do with the government’s stance and commitment at the federal level. Fahmi was responding to questions about whether political developments in Johor and Negeri Sembilan could affect the Unity Government’s stability.

items.title: Care home resident died from head trauma after alleged beating, police say
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 6 — Police have confirmed that a 54-year-old man died at a care home in Taman Choong Kwee, Tanjung Rambutan, on Tuesday, due to blunt force trauma to the head. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said a forensic specialist from Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital confirmed the cause after an autopsy was carried out yesterday. He was speaking at a press conference following a rank conferment ceremony for the Perak Commercial Crime Investigation Department chief and a handover of the Taiping district police chief’s post today.

items.title: MyCreative: Grants open to help artists break into global market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians are encouraged to tap available government financial support to expand their reach and elevate the local creative industry, said MyCreative Ventures group chief executive officer Zainol Haqim Zainol Rashid. "Under the Creative Content Fund, we offer the Marketability Fund, where artists looking to produce a new album can apply for financial support. Zainol said applications for the Creative Content Fund for the music sector are open until mid-September, adding that local artists invited to perform abroad can also seek financial backing.

items.title: Aeon Bank integrates MyTentera ID for seamless digital onboarding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aeon Bank has integrated MyTentera ID into its electronic know-your-customer (eKYC) verification process, allowing Malaysian armed forces personnel to complete identity verification seamlessly during digital banking onboarding. Aeon Bank said the move reinforces its commitment to providing inclusive, convenient and customer-focused digital banking solutions for Malaysians. Following successful onboarding, customers can access the bank's suite of Shariah-compliant products and services, including Savings Account-i, Aeon Bank x Visa Debit Card-i, Term Deposit-i, Savings Pot, DuitNow QR, Zakat, Takaful, JomPAY, utility bill payments and digital payment services through Aeon Bank's strategic partners and merchant network.

items.title: Syndicates switch to trains to smuggle drugs, say Thai police
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Thai police believe drug syndicates from Malaysia and several neighbouring countries have changed their smuggling tactics, including using trains to transport drugs out of Thailand to evade detection by authorities. He said police believe the change was prompted by intensified enforcement operations against drug trafficking networks by Thai authorities. Waesamae said Thai police would continue strengthening intelligence sharing and enforcement efforts to disrupt cross-border drug trafficking networks and bring those responsible to justice.

items.title: UK's Harworth gets US$784mil takeover bid from top investor Peel Holdings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Peel Holdings has offered to buy British land and property regeneration company Harworth Group in a deal valuing the London-listed firm at about £582.9 million (US$784.41 million), the real estate investor said on Thursday. Peel Holdings, part of British businessman John Whittaker's Peel Group, is the largest shareholder at Harworth with a nearly 30 per cent stake. Peel Holdings is offering 172.5 pence in cash per Harworth share for the shares it does not already own.

items.title: Penang Education Department launches probe after student allegedly targeted in sexual harassment, AI-manipulated images case
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 6 — The Penang State Education Department (JPNPP) has launched an internal investigation into an incident involving a female secondary school student who was allegedly subjected to sexual harassment and cyberbullying. “The department’s immediate priority is to protect the student involved. Yesterday, the mother of a Form Five student appealed for justice after alleging that her daughter had been subjected to sexual bullying and cyber harassment since April.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan’s new exco line-up to take oath at Seri Menanti tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 6 — Negeri Sembilan’s new state executive council line-up is scheduled to be sworn in before Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Besar Seri Menanti tomorrow morning. Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) formed the new state government after securing 25 of the 36 seats contested in Saturday’s 16th state election. BN won 18 seats and PN seven, giving the two coalitions a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.

items.title: Penang urged to enforce safety checks for ageing heritage buildings after Armenian Street incident
items.summary: ATAP chairman Datuk Ch’ng Huck Theng said guidelines and regulations should be introduced to ensure all heritage and pre-war buildings within the Unesco-listed site are safe. He said affordability could be an issue for some property owners, and the state government could provide grants to assist them. Apart from grants, Ch’ng said state authorities could consider other incentives, such as discounts on assessment fees or quit rent for owners who restore their pre-war properties.

items.title: Caregiver allegedly told residents to tie up man before fatal beating at Perak care home, police say
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 6 — A caregiver at a care home in Tanjung Rambutan allegedly instructed several residents to tie up a 54-year-old man before he was beaten to death, police said. The Star reported Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin as saying that initial investigations found the incident occurred late on Aug 3 after the victim allegedly became aggressive and disturbed other residents at the care home. Mohd Alwi said the victim was one of 21 residents at the care home.

items.title: Married couple among seven nabbed as police seize 2.8kg of MDMA in Perak raids
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 6 — Police arrested seven people, including a married couple, suspected of being involved in a drug trafficking syndicate that has been active since June in four separate raids in Ipoh and Tapah. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said they arrested the suspects - five men and two women aged between 22 and 44 - between 12.30 am and 3.05 am on Tuesday (Aug 4). He said this at a media conference after the rank-pinning ceremony for the Perak Commercial Crime Investigation Department chief and the handing-over ceremony for the Taiping district police chief at the Senior Police Officers’ Mess here today.

items.title: Fahmi calls for stronger cybersecurity, trusted AI adoption to drive Malaysia’s digital future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Industry players are encouraged to strengthen cybersecurity, promote responsible artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, share best practices and build trusted digital capabilities that would benefit Malaysia for years to come, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said as digital technologies become increasingly embedded across every sector of the economy, trust, security and resilience must advance in tandem with innovation. “As more organisations embrace digital technologies, trust will become just as important as innovation,” he said at the launch of U Mobile Enterprise Innovation Platform Hub here today.

items.title: Penang ranks third in international hotel guests, records nearly one million visitors in Q1 2026
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 6 — Penang ranked third in Malaysia for international hotel guests in the first quarter of 2026, recording 967,742 visitors, said state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai. He said Penang was behind Selangor, which recorded 1,051,718 international hotel guests, and Kuala Lumpur with 3,006,280 guests. “Tourism has always been one of the key pillars of Penang’s economy,” he said.

items.title: Pahang records over RM3m losses from telecom infrastructure vandalism, thefts
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 6 — Pahang continues to record a high number of vandalism and theft cases involving telecommunication infrastructure equipment, with total losses last year standing at over RM3 million. State Communications and Multimedia, Youth, Sports and Non-Governmental Organisation Committee chairman Datuk Fadzli Mohamad Kamal said the thefts, among others, led to communication disruptions in those areas, thereby affecting daily consumer affairs. He added that cables, batteries, communication equipment cards, diesel and Remote Radio Units are among the items stolen from communication infrastructure.

items.title: Malaysia’s services producer prices accelerate to 2.9pc growth in Q2 2026, says DOSM
items.summary: Accommodation and food and beverage services recorded the highest increase among the major subsectors, rising 6.4 per cent from a year earlier after growing 5.7 per cent in the previous quarter. Transportation was the second-fastest growing component, rising 5.6 per cent year-on-year compared with 3.8 per cent in the first quarter, largely due to a 17.5 per cent increase in passenger air transport prices. Real estate activities increased 0.6 per cent during the quarter, followed by education (0.5 per cent), health (0.3 per cent), information and communication (0.2 per cent) and professional services (0.1 per cent).

items.title: Lorry driver charged with sexually assaulting two daughters in Seri Iskandar
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 6 — A lorry driver was charged in the Sessions Court here today with 21 counts of sexually assaulting his two biological daughters, aged 13 and 16, in Seri Iskandar. According to the charge sheets, he was accused of kissing the neck, touching and molesting the breasts and private parts of his 16-year-old daughter, as well as forcing her to perform oral sex on him. He was also accused of touching the private parts, molesting the breasts and rubbing the buttocks of his 13-year-old daughter, as well as forcing her to touch his private part.

items.title: Zahid says those involved in TH mismanagement must face consequences
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Umno will not tolerate any breach of trust or mismanagement involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said that anyone found involved in wrongdoing or mismanagement within government agencies and statutory bodies must be held accountable. A special parliamentary session to debate the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH will be held on Aug 11.

items.title: Selangor exco: Data centre growth not straining domestic water supply
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 6 — The demand for data centres in Selangor has so far not placed pressure on domestic water supply, particularly in densely populated areas, said state Investment, Trade and Mobility Committee chairman Ng Sze Han. He said the state government continues to emphasise sustainable data centre development that is balanced with environmental needs and the well-being of the people. “Air Selangor also continuously reviews future water requirements for data centres, with projected future demand estimated at 632MLD,” he said.

items.title: Another suspected human skeleton found in gunny sack in Perlis, murder probe underway
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 6 — Police are investigating the discovery of another set of suspected human bones found protruding from a rotted white gunny sack in an overgrown area at Bohor Mali, near here. Kangar District Police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said police received a report from a 61-year-old man at 12.35 pm yesterday. Yusharifuddin said further investigations uncovered additional bones, along with a worn pair of boxer shorts, torn shorts and a belt.

items.title: Pahang orders immediate action on hazardous trees after deadly Janda Baik incident
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 6 — The Pahang government has directed all relevant agencies to hold immediate discussions to address the issue of hazardous trees following the tree-fall incident that claimed four lives in Janda Baik, Bentong, last Tuesday. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the discussions were aimed at coordinating action and identifying other high-risk locations to enable preventive measures to be taken to avoid similar incidents in the future. Wan Rosdy said trees identified as posing a risk would be assessed before appropriate action was taken, including felling them if necessary.

items.title: Amir Hamzah: Govt to unlock markets, private capital must drive investment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The government’s role is to maintain a credible policy and fiscal framework while using public capital to unlock markets, enabling private capital to play a larger role in driving investment, Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said. He said that while the government can provide policy certainty and maintain a credible fiscal framework, financing innovation and business expansion must increasingly be undertaken by banks, institutional investors, venture capital firms and private equity players. Amir Hamzah said venture capital could take the earliest risks, growth capital and private equity could finance expansion, banks would play a bigger role as companies’ cash flows strengthened, and public markets would provide another source of capital as companies matured.

items.title: Missing couple and son detained in Kubang Pasu over alleged RM25,000 ‘kutu’ scam
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 6 — A husband and wife, previously reported missing together with their nine-year-old son, have been detained for allegedly operating a fraudulent ‘kutu’ scheme. Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the couple, aged 36 and 39, surrendered at the Kubang Pasu district police headquarters at about 1.30 am today. Police had previously confirmed receiving a report on the disappearance of a family of three, including their nine-year-old son, which went viral on social media recently.

items.title: After Johor and Negeri Sembilan wins, Zahid sees ‘blue wave’ heading to Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said a “blue wave” could extend beyond Johor and Negeri Sembilan and soon reach Putrajaya, following Barisan Nasional’s (BN) strong showing in the two state elections. “The blue wave will continue. From Johor to Negeri Sembilan, and God willing, arrive here.

items.title: Zahid claims ministry officers ‘pressured’ over attending BN-linked events during state polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today alleged that some officers from his ministry had been “pressured” by “top people” in the government for attending events linked to Barisan Nasional (BN) during campaigning for the recent state elections. However, Zahid said his ministry’s officers were present only as part of their official duties. Zahid is BN chairman and Umno president.

items.title: MRT Corp awards RM3.03b Penang Mutiara LRT systems contract to MRCB-Theta Edge JV
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 6 — MRT Corp has awarded a RM3.028 billion system turnkey contract for the Penang Mutiara LRT Line, marking the project’s next major phase in the construction of Penang’s first Light Rail Transit (LRT) system. “The appointment will enable detailed design of the railway systems to proceed in parallel with the ongoing civil construction programme, ensuring both components remain aligned towards overall project delivery,” said MRT Corp in a statement today. MRT Corp said the Penang Mutiara LRT Line has continued to make steady progress through a series of key delivery milestones covering engineering design, construction planning, land readiness and railway systems implementation.

items.title: Johor MB launches Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme to boost mosque attendance
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 6 — The Johor government has introduced the Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme to be implemented at mosques across the state as part of efforts to strengthen the culture of congregational prayers, enliven mosques and foster syiar Islam (the propagation of Islamic values and teachings). Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the programme reflected the state government’s commitment to ensuring that mosques continued to serve as centres of worship, knowledge dissemination, and the strengthening of ukhuwah (brotherhood) among Muslims. He said the initiative was also among the Barisan Nasional manifesto pledges for the 16th Johor state election and would be implemented to fulfil the mandate entrusted by the people.

items.title: C4 calls for clearer mandate, transparency in MACC-Customs dept task force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Malaysia needs stronger transparency and accountability mechanisms to ensure government agencies can be effectively scrutinised by the public, said the Centre to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center). He was commenting on the proposed special task force between the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) to address revenue leakages at ports. The anti-corruption watchdog said efforts to strengthen enforcement should also be supported by wider institutional reforms to improve transparency and accountability within government agencies.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan meets UN resident coordinator to discuss Malaysia-UN cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan received a courtesy call from United Nations Resident Coordinator (UNRC) for Malaysia Nikolas Myint at Wisma Putra yesterday. In a Facebook post, Mohamad said the meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on cooperation between Malaysia and the United Nations. Myint was appointed as the UNRC for Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei by the United Nations Secretary-General on May 31, 2026.

items.title: KTMB services disrupted after lorry carrying flammable liquid causes power outage on Kulai-Kempas route
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 6 — The Shuttle Selatan and Electric Train Service (ETS) operations on the Kulai–Kempas route were disrupted yesterday following a power supply outage caused by a lorry carrying flammable liquid that skidded near the railway tracks. “For affected ETS passengers, shuttle bus services will be provided at Kulai, Kempas Baru, and JB Sentral stations. Fare adjustments will be provided to affected passengers,” it said.
